title: Chemistry-resolved disagreement between Materials Project-compatible PBE(+U) and r2SCAN stability verdicts in the GNoME materials database
abstract: arXiv:2610.33101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GNoME's stability labels rest on a Materials Project-compatible GGA/GGA+U workflow. Its authors report that 84% of discovered binaries and ternaries retain a negative decomposition energy under r2SCAN and 86.8% of tested quaternaries remain stable on the r2SCAN hull. We resolve that aggregate by chemistry over the 139,541 GNoME materials released with r2SCAN recomputations, a subset the dataset authors selected rather than sampled, using cluster bootstrap intervals over 8,429 structural-prototype proxy clusters. The aggregate conceals a 26.7-point spread at fixed element count, from 4.0% [3.3, 4.7] for plain quaternary intermetallics (no lanthanide, no 3d metal) to 30.7% [27.7, 33.8] for lanthanide-free 3d-containing quaternary oxides, a pair identified post hoc against a prospectively fixed threshold. Under our reading of the release's "All" reference set the two cells sit at 14.5% and 37.4%, preserving a 22.9-point spread. Presence of a Materials Project Hubbard-U-list element is strongly associated with disagreement, conditional on the other covariates, in a model over all 139,541 materials (cluster-robust odds ratio 3.45 [3.13, 3.80]). Neither selective U application nor hull proximity explains the association away: disagreement stays elevated outside the U-treated regime, and a natural cubic spline in the continuous PBE decomposition energy moves the odds ratio in the 117,018-material model only from 3.53 to 3.43 [3.07, 3.83]. For allocating a verification budget, composition supplements hull proximity rather than replacing it: over held-out cluster splits at a 20% budget, the two together surface 45.8% of disagreements against 40.4% for hull distance alone. An exploratory comparison against previously catalogued materials changes direction between populations. We measure disagreement between two workflows, not accuracy.
summary:
- GNoME’s PBE(+U)-based stability labels conflict with r2SCAN predictions for many materials.
- Disagreement varies by chemistry: ~4 % for plain quaternary intermetallics versus ~31 % for lanthanide‑free 3d‑containing quaternary oxides.
- Materials with a Materials Project Hubbard‑U element show a ~5× higher odds of disagreement, independent of U application or hull proximity.

title: On the Doppler Effect in Static Materials: Vortices and Black, White and Worm-Hole Like Wave Trajectories
abstract: arXiv:2610.33141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the Doppler effect in a static material. The effect is achieved with a network of thin waveguides whose lengths depend on the direction of travel, chosen to simulate the compression and expansion of the wave experienced by a source travelling with velocity $v$. Each edge of length $\ell$ becomes a pair of waveguides of lengths $\ell/(1\mp v/c)$, one for each direction of travel. On a lattice this gives the field pattern of a moving source. To demonstrate the effect, we design a vortex, an analogue black hole and wormhole.
summary:
- Demonstrates Doppler effect in a static material by using direction‑dependent waveguide lengths ℓ/(1∓v/c).
- Implements a lattice of paired waveguides to reproduce the field pattern of a moving source.
- Realizes vortex, black‑hole, and wormhole analogues to illustrate wave trajectories.

title: The Ising lattice gas and the surface diffusion of CO on Cu(001) at finite coverage
abstract: arXiv:2610.33147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The memory equation of the coherent intermediate scattering function (ISF), derived previously for lattice gases, is applied to the Ising lattice gas under Kawasaki dynamics. The ISF follows the decay of a density wave of adparticles, a superposition of exponential relaxation modes: the decay starts at a rate fixed by a sum rule and is then slowed by a memory. The static structure factor and the effective hop rate are obtained in closed form, exactly along a one-dimensional channel; with the sum rule they give a single exponential, a lower bound on the ISF. Exact relaxation spectra show that this single exponential, built from equilibrium quantities alone, reproduces the correlation time only at weak coupling; only there can a measured dephasing rate be read through the statics. For strong attraction the slow dissolution of clusters lengthens the correlation time up to ninefold, whereas a repulsive layer relaxes nearly as a single mode at its structure peak. The dephasing rate, fitted over a time window where it is nearly constant, approaches the slowest relaxation rate, not the initial one; the sum rule reaches the data only through the area beneath the normalized decay, which defines the correlation time. For CO/Cu(001), the lattice gas reproduces the dephasing rates measured along two crystal directions and requires a nearest-neighbour repulsion of at least $35$--$50$~meV, whatever the jump rates; the measured rate is then close to the inverse correlation time, and the memory is predicted to grow with coverage.
summary:
- Applied memory equation to Ising lattice gas (Kawasaki dynamics) → ISF decays as superposition of exponential modes, bounded by a sum‑rule‑determined initial rate.
- Derived closed‑form static structure factor and effective hop rate (exact in 1D); single‑exponential bound reproduces correlation time only at weak coupling, while strong attraction lengthens it up to ~9×.
- Modeled CO/Cu(surface diffusion: lattice‑gas fit requires nearest‑neighbour repulsion 35–50 meV to match measured dephasing rates along two crystal directions.

title: Cooperation of itinerant and localized physics in the magnetic phase diagram of 214 Ruddlesden-Popper iridates
authors: Francesco Cassol, Michele Casula, Benjamin Lenz
abstract: arXiv:2610.33196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $5d^5$ Ruddlesden-Popper iridates Sr$_2$IrO$_4$ and Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ have attracted considerable attention as spin-orbit entangled analogues of the cuprates, yet the origin of their antiferromagnetic insulating state, of Slater or of Mott-Heisenberg type, remains debated. We find that both materials sit in an intermediate regime in which itinerant and localized electrons cooperate in stabilizing the antiferromagnetic order, with Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ slightly more correlated than Sr$_2$IrO$_4$. We obtain this by computing, within dynamical mean-field theory, the interaction-temperature phase diagram of a realistic three-orbital $t_{2g}$ Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling. Our study shows that neither the behavior of the gap across the N\'eel temperature nor the spin-polaron features of the spectral function unambiguously identify the cooperative regime, whereas the two-peak structure of the optical conductivity is reproduced only there and therefore constitutes a reliable fingerprint. By placing both compounds in a common phase diagram, our results reconcile seemingly contradictory experimental and theoretical reports, and provide a unified framework for future studies of the 214 iridates and of other spin-orbit coupled correlated materials.
summary:
- Sr₂IrO₄ and Ba₂IrO₄ occupy an intermediate regime where itinerant and localized electrons cooperate to stabilize antiferromagnetism.
- DMFT on a realistic three‑orbital t₂g Hubbard model with spin‑orbit coupling shows Ba₂IrO₄ is slightly more correlated than Sr₂IrO₄.
- Only the two‑peak structure in the optical conductivity unambiguously signals this cooperative regime; gap evolution and spin‑polaron features do not.

title: Orbital Hall response of spin-1 fermions with a curved central band
authors: J. H. Warnes, Dayana Joy, Pankaj Bhalla, Rhonald Burgos Atencia
abstract: arXiv:2610.33211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the orbital Hall effect in a three-band system described by a low-energy Hamiltonian containing both linear and quadratic momentum-dependent contributions. The linear term lifts the degeneracy between the dispersive bands, providing a minimal setting to study orbital transport in a multiband system with a curved central band. Within a quantum kinetic approach, we derive the intrinsic orbital Hall response and analyze its microscopic origin in terms of interband coherence induced by an external electric field. We show that the orbital Hall conductivity arises from the interplay between the momentum-dependent orbital character of the eigenstates and transitions between different bands. The spin-1 structure provides a particularly transparent platform in which the contributions associated with different interband channels can be identified separately. We further show that the differential orbital Hall response provides a direct probe of the low-energy structure, exhibiting distinct scaling singularities associated with the linear and quadratic bands, respectively, while remaining independent of the ultraviolet cutoff. Our results establish a connection between the multiband quantum geometry of spin-1 fermions and their transverse orbital response, and provide a simple framework for investigating orbital transport beyond two-band models.
summary:
- Derived intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity for a spin‑1 fermion model with linear and quadratic momentum terms, attributing the response to interband coherence.
- Found differential orbital Hall response exhibits distinct scaling singularities from linear and quadratic bands, independent of ultraviolet cutoff.
- Established that the multiband quantum geometry of spin‑1 fermions dictates transverse orbital transport, extending analysis beyond two‑band models.

title: Evolution of microstructure and crystallographic texture in a novel Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy during hot rotary swaging
authors: Adam Strnad, Jana \v{S}milauerov\'a, Josef Str\'ask\'y, Luk\'a\v{s} Hor\'ak, Jan \v{C}apek, Al\v{z}b\v{e}ta Endrychov\'a, Martin Hol\v{c}\'ak, Ji\v{r}\'i Z\'yka, Milo\v{s} Jane\v{c}ek, Petr Harcuba
abstract: arXiv:2610.33247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A multi-step induction-assisted hot rotary swaging route was developed for the novel dual-phase Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy to investigate the evolution of microstructure, crystallographic texture, and mechanical properties during sequential deformation. Phase-transformation temperatures determined by electrical resistivity measurements were used to select processing conditions in the single-phase $\beta$ field at 880{\deg}C and the $\alpha+\beta$ field at 780{\deg}C. Induction heating with thermographic temperature control enabled reduction of the initial 12 mm rod to 6.3 mm, corresponding to a total area reduction of 72%. Swaging in the $\beta$ field refined millimetre-sized prior-$\beta$ grains to approximately 100 $\mu$m, while subsequent cooling produced a fine lamellar $\alpha+\beta$ microstructure. Further deformation in the $\alpha+\beta$ field disrupted the lamellar structure, promoted globularisation and recrystallisation of the $\alpha$ phase, and refined the $\beta$ phase. The microstructural evolution was accompanied by a pronounced $\langle 11\bar{2}0\rangle_{\alpha}\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ fibre texture in the $\alpha$ phase, whereas the $\beta$ phase exhibited predominantly $\langle 110\rangle_{\beta}\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ together with a $\langle 111\rangle_{\beta}\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ component. The phase constitution remained comparatively stable, with approximately 12-15 wt.% retained $\beta$ throughout processing. Subsequent $\alpha+\beta$ swaging decreased the compressive yield strength from 1103 to 839 MPa while increasing plastic deformability, with a maximum fracture strain of 32%. Radial hardness heterogeneity was progressively eliminated. These results demonstrate that induction-assisted rotary swaging in selected phase fields provides an effective route for tailoring microstructure, texture, and mechanical response in dual-phase zirconium alloys.
summary: - Multi‑step induction‑assisted hot rotary swaging at 880 °C (β) and 780 °C (α+β) reduced a 12 mm rod to 3 mm (72 % area reduction).

title: Winding-Controlled Topological Descendants of Antialtermagnets
authors: Sahar Izadi Vishkayi, Carmine Autieri, Meysam Bagheri Tagani
abstract: arXiv:2610.33252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Odd-parity spin splitting constrains magnetic band crossings but does not determine their topological descendants. We show that the Chern contribution of an isolated inverted sector is controlled by the phase winding of its transverse mass pair: when the masses and tangential velocities reverse together, contributions from successive Dirac points add rather than cancel. This distinguishes topological winding from the polynomial degree labeling the magnetic parent. For specified complementary masses, periodic tetragonal $h$- and hexagonal $j$-wave models host eight and twelve same-chirality Weyl points on a momentum plane, with gapped-slice Chern numbers $|C|=4$ and $6$, respectively. A microscopic four-band $p$-wave model identifies an antiunitary obstruction to first-order transverse masses and demonstrates a symmetry-broken $C=1$ phase at quarter filling. First-principles calculations for the proposed coplanar spin-vortex texture of LaMnAu$_5$ reveal the $h$-wave nodal pattern, its anisotropic spin--orbit reconstruction, and a mirror-channel spectral response that reverses under opposite spin rotations. Together, these results distinguish the symmetry of an odd-parity magnetic parent from the mass structure controlling the topology of its descendants.
summary:
- Phase winding of transverse masses dictates additive Chern contributions of Dirac points.
- h‑wave

title: Unified First-Principles Theory of Finite-Wave-Vector Photocurrents in Crystals
authors: Bumseop Kim, Sayed Ali Akbar Ghorashi, Yicong Chen, Ritesh Agarwal, Andrew M. Rappe
abstract: arXiv:2610.33264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatially structured light carries independent phase and envelope variations in addition to its polarization and frequency. We develop a first-principles theory of second-order dc photocurrents (especially shift and injection) that resolves how these optical degrees of freedom drive distinct dc responses in crystals. The second-order dc response couples two optical field components at the same frequency but with generally different wave vectors. Expanding the response to first order in these wave vectors identifies two rank-four material tensors: $\xi$, which couples to the optical phase gradient and contains the plane-wave photon-drag limit, and $\zeta$, which couples to the intensity gradient and describes a spatially varying dc current. Wannier-interpolated calculations for monolayer GeS show symmetry-allowed finite-wave-vector responses that survive at a centrosymmetric structure where conventional bulk photovoltaic effect vanishes. For a Gaussian beam with a uniform phase gradient, the phase-gradient contribution drives current in the same direction on both sides of the beam center, whereas the intensity-gradient contribution drives currents in opposite directions, showing that distinct photocurrent patterns can be selected through the wavefront and envelope of light. A multipolar analysis further resolves the optical corrections into electric-quadrupole, orbital magnetic-dipole, and band-dispersion contributions. Together, these results show how the spatial structure of light can serve as an independent control variable for nonlinear photocurrent generation and provide a first-principles route to predict this response in real materials.
summary: - First‑principles theory of second‑order dc photocurrents driven by spatially structured light, introducing tensors ξ (phase‑gradient) and ζ

title: Chern non-trivial two-dimensional square-net nodal line semimetal
authors: Kendall Ramos, Salvador Barraza-Lopez, Elias Andrade
abstract: arXiv:2610.33303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional $p_xp_y$ square-net tight-binding model with two sublattices and introduce a symmetry-informed, momentum-dependent spin-orbit coupling (SOC) with a finite-range real-space hopping representation. Its two components jointly gap the nodal line, while one breaks time-reversal symmetry, producing a Chern-insulating phase with an occupied band Chern number $C=2$. Nanoribbon calculations reveal edge-localized states traversing this gap, with two net chiral modes per edge. We further show that the conserved spin sectors are unitarily equivalent and therefore have equal Chern numbers, ruling out a nontrivial time-reversal-protected $\mathbb{Z}_2$ phase within this ansatz. Our results establish a phenomenological route to Chern topology in square-net two-dimensional systems and clarify the symmetry constraints governing the accessible insulating phases.
summary:
- 2D \(p_xp_y\) square‑net tight‑binding model with two sublattices and momentum‑dependent SOC gaps a nodal line.
- SOC breaks time‑reversal symmetry, producing a Chern insulator with \(C=2\) and two chiral edge modes per edge.
- Spin sectors are unitarily equivalent, ruling out a \(\mathbb{Z}_2\) phase and clarifying symmetry constraints for Chern topology.

title: Exploring Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures for Self-Supervised Representation Learning of Powder X-ray Diffraction Patterns
abstract: arXiv:2610.33310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) is the primary high-throughput method for resolving crystal structures, a cornerstone of materials science. As high-throughput synthesis and self-driving laboratories advance, automated XRD pattern analysis has become vital for accelerating materials discovery. However, traditional matrix factorization methods fail when lattice variations cause non-linear peak shifts. At the same time, supervised learning approaches face a combinatorial explosion when handling multi-phase mixtures. To overcome these challenges, we adopt a self-supervised Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to learn representation embeddings from 1D diffraction patterns. By optimizing a masked self-prediction loss directly within the latent space, the framework captures high-level crystallographic semantics. Downstream evaluations show that lightweight attentive probes trained on frozen JEPA representations achieve space group classification and lattice parameter estimation accuracy close to much larger supervised vision transformers. Furthermore, latent probing reveals that the learned representation space naturally organizes physical transformations, isolating smooth trajectories for peak broadening. Interestingly, decoding along latent paths between single-phase crystal representations yields realistic multi-phase mixture patterns, demonstrating an emergent continuous structure learned without explicit multi-phase supervision.
summary:
- Self‑supervised Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) learns 1‑D XRD embeddings via masked latent‑space prediction.
- Frozen JEPA representations enable lightweight probes to match large supervised vision‑transformer accuracy for space‑group classification and lattice‑parameter estimation.
- Latent space naturally orders crystallographic transformations; interpolations generate realistic multi‑phase diffraction patterns without explicit supervision.

title: Exact Magnetic Confinement of a Doped Hole by Kinetic Frustration
authors: Nikolai Peshcherenko, Yixin Zhang, Cristian D. Batista, Yang Zhang
abstract: arXiv:2610.33585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an exact mechanism of magnetic confinement driven purely by kinetic frustration. In a finite open sawtooth $U=\infty$ Hubbard chain of $L$ unit cells doped with one hole, the ground state at magnetization $M$ contains $M$ polarized triplet dimers surrounding a connected singlet region of length $\ell_{\rm s}=L-M$. A magnetic field selects $M$ and hence the confinement length. The hole forms a standing wave in the singlet region with exponential tails in the triplet background. Confinement requires neither disorder nor an exchange-generated string tension: destructive interference between direct and apex-mediated hopping makes the triplet bonds reflecting. At $t_2/t_1=[2+4\cos(\pi/(\ell_{\rm s}+2))]^{-1/2}$, they become perfectly reflecting, producing a position-degenerate compact localized state. At every fixed field $0<h_{\rm sat}$, the singlet region remains finite as $L\to\infty$ and shrinks stepwise with increasing field, whereas at $h=0$ it spans the system.
summary:
- Kinetic frustration in a sawtooth Hubbard chain exactly confines a doped hole, creating a singlet region surrounded by polarized triplet dimers.
- The confinement length equals the magnetization \(M\); the hole forms a standing wave with exponential tails, and triplet bonds become perfectly reflecting at \(t_2/t_1=[2+4\cos(\pi/(\ell_{\rm s}+)]^{-1/2}\).
- A magnetic field selects \(M\), shrinking the singlet region stepwise; at \(h=0\) it spans the system, while for any \(h>0\) it remains finite as

title: Tuning from intrinsic to disorder-dominated quantum states in a kagome antiferromagnet
authors: Y. Tanaka, R. Kumakura, T. Yamaguchi, M. Kato, K. Totsuka, B. Li, Y. Zhao, Y. Li, R. Grasset, O. Cavani, A. Alessi, V. Sharma, Y. Kohama, S. Suetsugu
abstract: arXiv:2610.34230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet (AFM) provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing quantum spin-liquid (QSL) and magnetization-plateau states. Experimental progress, however, has been hindered by structural disorder, whose effects on these quantum states remain elusive. A key experimental challenge is therefore to connect intrinsic and disorder-dominated regimes through controlled disorder and identify emergent degrees of freedom associated with disorder. Here we introduce controlled point defects through electron irradiation into the spin-1/2 kagome AFM YCu3(OH)6.5Br2.5 (YCOB) and track the resulting evolution of its low-energy magnetic states. High-field magnetic torque measurements reveal that the 1/9 and 1/3 magnetization plateaus are strongly suppressed by only ~0.05% irradiation-induced defects, demonstrating that these delicate quantum many-body states are extraordinarily fragile against dilute disorder. Moreover, the irradiation induces a sign reversal of the magnetic torque only at low temperatures and low fields, indicating the emergence of correlated defect-induced moments rather than isolated free spins. Remarkably, the characteristic scaling of the magnetic specific heat, absent in pristine YCOB, progressively emerges with increasing disorder. These findings establish dilute disorder as an effective tuning parameter that drives the kagome AFM from intrinsic quantum states toward a disorder-dominated regime. The contrasting responses further identify pristine YCOB as an exceptionally clean kagome AFM for accessing intrinsic quantum states.
summary:
- ~05 % irradiation defects collapse 1/9 and 1/3 magnetization plateaus, showing extreme fragility of kagome QSL states.
- Defects form correlated moments that reverse

title: Controllable charge-spin conversion in sliding multiferroic metal Fe3GaTe2
authors: Tongrui Li, Lidong Zhang, Weiyi Pan
abstract: arXiv:2610.34295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling charge--spin conversion within a single magnetic material is important for compact spintronic devices. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, and Wannier-based linear response, we study the Edelstein and spin Hall responses of sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2}. Two degenerate ground states with opposite interlayer sliding vectors and out-of-plane dipole moments are separated by a calculated switching barrier of about $16.3$~meV per unit cell. Magnetization orientation determines the allowed current-induced spin components, while ferroelectric switching induces component-selective sign reversals governed by $M_z\mathcal T$ for in-plane magnetization and by $M_z$ for out-of-plane magnetization. The Edelstein response is strongly energy dependent, with spin accumulation approaching $2~\hbar$ for $\mathbf m\parallel+y$ under a reference field of $1$~V/\AA. Momentum-resolved analysis links the TR-even and TR-odd Edelstein responses to $\Gamma$-centered constant-energy contours and localized interband features, respectively. Spin-conductivity contributions show the opposite momentum-space character, with broad sign-competing spin Berry curvature for TR-even and narrow Fermi-surface contours for TR-odd. The transverse spin Hall conductivity reaches $\sim10^{3}\,(\hbar/e)(\mathrm{S/cm})$ and depends strongly on ferroelectric state and magnetization direction. Magnetization rotations in the $xy$ and $xz$ planes reveal symmetry-allowed higher angular harmonics in both spin accumulation and spin-current responses. These results establish sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2} as a tunable platform for reconfigurable spin accumulation and spin-current generation.
summary:
- Fe₃GaTe₂ bilayer exhibits controllable Edelstein and spin‑Hall effects driven by interlayer sliding and magnetization orientation.
- Two degenerate sliding states (ΔE ≈ 3 meV) switch the sign of spin responses via symmetry \(M_z\mathcal T\) or \(M_z\).
- Edelstein spin accumulation reaches ~2 ħ and spin‑Hall conductivity ≈ 10³ (ħ/e) S/cm, both highly tunable by ferroelectric state and magnetization direction.

title: Fermionic superfluid transition and pairing scale separation in the kagome flat band
abstract: arXiv:2610.34342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flat-band systems provide a promising platform for exploring exotic correlated phases owing to quenched kinetic energy and enhanced interaction effects. In this work, we investigate the flat-band superfluid transition in the attractive kagome Hubbard model using large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations accelerated by fast Fourier transforms and delay updates. Through systematic calculations of the transition temperature, spin susceptibility, and density compressibility, we establish the finite-temperature phase diagram at the flat-band filling $\rho=5/3$ and find a clear linear scaling of the superfluid transition temperature with the interaction strength, $T_{\mathrm{c}}=0.0314|U|$. Our results reveal a wide separation of temperature scales between local pair formation and global phase coherence, which stabilizes a broad intermediate supercompressible bosonic fluid region of preformed pairs that bridges the normal Fermi gas and the flat-band superfluid. We further demonstrate that both the transition temperature and density compressibility are significantly enhanced in the flat band compared to van Hove fillings. Our findings highlight the essential role of flat-band-enhanced pair-density fluctuations in separating the pairing and phase-coherence scales, offering clear experimental signatures for probing flat-band superfluidity and superconductivity in cold-atom and kagome-material platforms.
summary:
- Tc scales linearly with interaction strength: \(T_c = 0314|U|\) at flat‑band filling \(\rho=5/3\).
- Large separation between local pair formation and global phase coherence creates a supercompressible pre‑formed‑pair fluid.
- Flat band boosts both \(T_c\) and density compressibility versus van Hove fillings, due to enhanced pair‑density fluctuations.

title: Theory of the $1/9$ Magnetization Plateau of the Spin-$1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet
abstract: arXiv:2610.34439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the $1/9$ magnetization plateau of the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet using infinite projected entangled-pair states and identify a spin-density-wave state with a $27$-site unit cell and a lower variational energy than previous approaches. In contrast to higher-magnetization plateaus, which are well described by localized magnons on nonoverlapping hexagons and preserve a sixfold rotational symmetry, the $1/9$ plateau only keeps a threefold rotational symmmetry and consists of a tiling by three types of $9$-site clusters related by $\pm2\pi/3$ rotations. These conclusions are supported by a complementary cluster mean-field theory which correctly preserves the symmetry of the higher plateaus but leads to the same spontaneous symmetry breaking for the $1/9$ plateau with a qualitatively similar pattern of nine different local magnetizations.
summary:
- Spin‑density‑wave state with a 27‑site unit cell found for the 1/9 plateau.
- Sixfold rotational symmetry is reduced to threefold, forming a tiling of three 9‑site clusters.
- Infinite PEPS and cluster mean‑field theory give lower energy and consistent local magnetization patterns.

title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
authors: Gabriele Bellomia, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Massimo Capone, Adriano Amaricci
abstract: arXiv:2610.34470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.
summary:
- Introduces symmetry‑resolved parity‑superselected two‑site entanglement measured by fermionic negativity and relative entropy of entanglement.
- Extends the resolution to full entanglement in pure and mixed states, applying it to the Hubbard dimer and plaquette CDMFT.
- Shows that the three symmetry‑resolved components track distinct aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics across interaction‑ and density‑driven transitions.

title: Quasiparticle Interactions in the $S = 1/2$ Heisenberg Antiferromagnetic Chain CuPzN
authors: Leshan Zhao, Timothy Reeder, Matthew Stone, Daniel G. Mazzone, Jakob Lass, Christof Niedermayer, Daniel H. Reich, Anna Keselman, Oleg A. Starykh, Collin Broholm
abstract: arXiv:2610.34536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate spinon--spinon interactions in the quasi-one-dimensional $S=1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet Cu(C$_4$H$_4$N$_2$)(NO$_3$)$_2$ (CuPzN) using inelastic neutron scattering. At zero field, the spectrum exhibits the canonical multi-spinon continuum of the Heisenberg chain. With increasing field we demonstrate the appearance of an energy gap $2\Delta$ towards momentum $q\rightarrow 0$ between the uniform magnetization precession mode and the shifted spinon continuum. $2\Delta$ is a direct measure of spinon backscattering interactions. Comparison with numerical matrix-product-state calculations and a recent analytical theory shows excellent agreement. By examining the integrable spin-1/2 chain, we provide an example of how quasiparticle interactions can be quantified experimentally in isotropic quantum spin systems.
summary:
- Spinon–spinon interactions in CuPzN measured by inelastic neutron scattering; zero‑field spectrum shows the standard multi‑spinon continuum.
- Magnetic field opens a gap \(2\Delta\) at \(q\!\to\!0\) between the uniform precession mode and the shifted continuum, directly quantifying backscattering.
- Experimental data match matrix‑product‑state simulations and analytic theory, validating experimental quantification of quasiparticle interactions in an isotropic spin‑½ chain.

title: Spontaneous magnetic diode effect in Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$
authors: Yining Hu, Taikang Chen, Jan Priessnitz, Zili Feng, Takashi Kurumaji, Linda Ye, Libor \v{S}mejkal, Chunyu Mark Guo, Philip J. W. Moll
abstract: arXiv:2610.34586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.
summary:
- Spontaneous magnetic diode effect observed in Co₁/₃TaS₂, where chiral lattice and reversible chiral magnetic order produce nonreciprocal resistance.
- Originates from a noncoplanar spin texture with zero net magnetization, driven by spin–orbit coupling and time‑reversal symmetry breaking.
- Reversing magnetic handedness flips diode polarity, enabling magnetic control of current direction without external fields.

title: Non-magnetic impurities as a quantum microscope of finite size effects in spin chains
authors: Quentin Faure, Shintaro Takayoshi, Virginie Simonet, B\'eatrice Grenier, St\'ephane Raymond, Eric Ressouche, Xavier Fabr\`eges, Pascal Lejay, Thierry Giamarchi, Sylvain Petit
abstract: arXiv:2610.34596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-size effects are ubiquitous in quantum matter, yet typically invisible in the thermodynamic limit; when system size is restricted, boundaries and confinement reveal modified spectra, correlations, and emergent phenomena. With growing access to well-controlled few-spin systems, these effects are now directly observable and offer a route to probing universal physics and enabling quantum information applications. Here, we study finite-size physics in the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet Ba(Co$_{1-x}$Mg$_x$)$_2$V$_2$O$_8$ with $x = 2\%$ and $x = 5\%$, where non-magnetic Mg$^{2+}$ ions fragment the Co$^{2+}$ spin chains into finite segments. Combining inelastic neutron scattering and numerical calculations, we identify distinct regimes with fundamentally different low-energy quantum excitations: spinons confined to chain boundaries, and a cluster mode in shorter chains corresponding to a collective reversal of the N\'eel-ordered segment without classical analogue. Our results demonstrate how chemical substitution acts as a quantum microscope providing direct access to boundary-shaped excitations in strongly correlated spin systems.
summary:
- Mg²⁺ impurities fragment Co²⁺ chains in Ba(Co₁₋ₓMgₓ)₂V₂O₈, creating finite spin‑chain segments.
- Neutron scattering shows two regimes: spinons confined to chain ends and a collective “cluster mode” in short chains.
- Chemical substitution serves as a quantum microscope, revealing boundary‑induced excitations in a quasi‑1D antiferromagnet.
